title: Deuteronomy Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Deuteronomy chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Deuteronomy Chapter 18.

questions.question: What inheritance do the priests, the Levites, and the tribe of Levi have among Israel?
options: They have no part nor inheritance with Israel
They inherit a portion of the land
questions.correctAnswer: They have no part nor inheritance with Israel
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:1 states that the priests, the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi shall have no part nor inheritance with Israel.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18, who is the inheritance of the Levites?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:2 says that the LORD is the inheritance of the Levites, so they have no inheritance among their brethren.

questions.question: From what animals are priests to receive the shoulder, two cheeks, and the maw as their due?
questions.correctAnswer: Ox and sheep
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:3 explains that priests receive these portions from sacrifices of ox or sheep.

questions.question: What firstfruits must be given to the priests according to Deuteronomy 18?
options: Corn, wine, oil, and fleece of sheep
questions.correctAnswer: Corn, wine, oil, and fleece of sheep
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:4 states that the firstfruits of corn, wine, oil, and the first of the fleece of sheep shall be given to the priests.

questions.question: Why did the LORD choose the Levites out of all the tribes of Israel?
options: To minister in His name forever
questions.correctAnswer: To minister in His name forever
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:5 explains that the LORD chose the Levites to stand and minister in His name forever.

questions.question: True or False: A Levite can come from any of the gates of Israel to minister at the place the LORD chooses.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:6 confirms that if a Levite comes from any gate where he sojourned in Israel to the chosen place, he can minister.

questions.question: What will a Levite do when he comes to the place the LORD chooses?
options: He shall minister in the name of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: He shall minister in the name of the LORD
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:7 states that the Levite shall minister in the name of the LORD his God as his brethren do.

questions.question: Besides what comes from the sale of his patrimony, what do Levites receive?
questions.correctAnswer: Like portions to eat
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:8 says that Levites shall have like portions to eat beside that which comes from the sale of his patrimony.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 18 forbids learning to do after the abominations of the nations that the LORD is giving to Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:9 commands not to learn the abominations of the nations the LORD is giving to Israel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as an abomination in Deuteronomy 18?
questions.correctAnswer: Usury
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:10-11 lists abominations such as divination, enchanters, and consulting with familiar spirits, but usury is not mentioned.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD drives out nations because they do these abominations.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:12 states that because of these abominations the LORD drives out those nations before Israel.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 18:13 command the people to be with the LORD their God?
questions.correctAnswer: Perfect
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:13 instructs the people to be perfect with the LORD their God.

questions.question: Who will the LORD raise up from among the brethren like unto Moses, according to Deuteronomy 18?
questions.correctAnswer: A Prophet
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:15 says the LORD will raise up a Prophet from among the brethren like Moses.

questions.question: What will happen to a prophet who presumptuously speaks a word in the name of the LORD that He has not commanded?
questions.correctAnswer: That prophet shall die
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:20 declares that any prophet who speaks presumptuously in God's name shall die.

questions.question: True or False: If a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the prophecy does not come to pass, the LORD has not spoken it.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:22 explains that if the prophecy does not come to pass, it is not of the LORD and the prophet spoke presumptuously.

medium.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Deuteronomy Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:9, what are the Israelites instructed not to learn when they enter the land given by the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: The abominations of those nations
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:9 specifically instructs the Israelites not to learn to do after the abominations of the nations they will possess, emphasizing separation from pagan practices.

questions.question: Which of the following practices is NOT listed in Deuteronomy 18:10 as forbidden among the Israelites?
options: Making children pass through the fire
questions.correctAnswer: Offering sacrifices
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:10 forbids practices such as divination, enchantment, and making children pass through the fire, but does not forbid offering sacrifices, which was a priestly duty.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:11, which of these is considered an abominable practice among the nations that the Israelites must avoid?
questions.correctAnswer: Consulting with familiar spirits
questions.explanation: Verse 11 lists consulting with familiar spirits among the forbidden practices, distinguishing it from acceptable worship practices like offering firstfruits or building altars.

questions.question: What consequence does Deuteronomy 18:12 say will happen because of the abominations practiced by other nations?
options: The LORD will drive them out before the Israelites
They will be blessed with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will drive them out before the Israelites
questions.explanation: Verse 12 explains that because of these abominations, the LORD will drive out those nations before the Israelites, showing divine judgment against such practices.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 18:13 encourages the Israelites to be 'perfect' with whom?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Verse 13 calls for the Israelites to be perfect with the LORD their God, emphasizing wholehearted obedience and faithfulness.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18:14 explain the difference between the Israelites and the nations they will possess?
options: The LORD has not suffered the Israelites to practice divination
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD has not suffered the Israelites to practice divination
questions.explanation: Verse 14 contrasts the nations who hearken to diviners with the Israelites, whom the LORD has not allowed to do so, highlighting a distinct divine prohibition.

questions.question: What promise does Deuteronomy 18:15 give concerning a prophet that the LORD will raise up?
options: A prophet like Moses from among their brethren
A prophet who will bring wealth
A prophet from a foreign land
A prophet who will establish a new law
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet like Moses from among their brethren
questions.explanation: Verse 15 promises that the LORD will raise up a Prophet like Moses from their brethren, emphasizing continuity in God's guidance.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:16, why did the Israelites desire not to hear the voice of the LORD again at Horeb?
options: Because the fire was so great they feared they might die
Because they did not believe Him
Because they wanted to worship other gods
Because they preferred Moses to speak for them
questions.correctAnswer: Because the fire was so great they feared they might die
questions.explanation: Verse 16 states the people requested not to hear the voice of the LORD again due to the fear caused by the great fire, showing their reverence and fear of God's power.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 18:17 record as God's response to the people's desire at Horeb?
options: God said they have spoken well
God commanded them to be silent
questions.correctAnswer: God said they have spoken well
questions.explanation: Verse 17 records that the LORD said the people had spoken well, acknowledging their fear and supporting the promise of a prophet to speak for Him.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18:18 describe the role of the prophet the LORD will raise up?
options: He will speak the words the LORD commands him
He will rule over the people
He will perform miracles to prove his authority
He will lead the people into battle
questions.correctAnswer: He will speak the words the LORD commands him
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that the LORD will put His words into the prophet’s mouth and he will speak all that God commands, emphasizing obedience and divine authority.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:19, what will happen to anyone who does not listen to the words spoken by the prophet in God's name?
options: God will require it of him
He will become a prophet himself
questions.correctAnswer: God will require it of him
questions.explanation: Verse 19 warns that God will hold accountable anyone who refuses to listen to the prophet’s words spoken in His name, emphasizing responsibility.

questions.question: What consequence does Deuteronomy 18:20 prescribe for a prophet who speaks presumptuously in God's name or speaks in the name of other gods?
questions.correctAnswer: That prophet shall die
questions.explanation: Verse 20 clearly states that any prophet who speaks presumptuously or in the name of other gods shall die, underscoring the seriousness of false prophecy.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18:21-22 instruct the people to discern a true prophet from a false one?
options: If the prophecy does not come to pass, the prophet has spoken presumptuously
If the prophet performs miracles, he is true
If the prophet speaks softly, he is false
If the prophet is popular among the people, he is true
questions.correctAnswer: If the prophecy does not come to pass, the prophet has spoken presumptuously
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 teach that a prophet’s word must come true; if it does not, the prophecy is from the prophet’s own presumption, not from God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Deuteronomy 18:13, the Israelites are commanded to be perfect with the LORD their God.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:13 explicitly commands the Israelites to be perfect with the LORD their God, calling for wholehearted faith and obedience.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 18:14 states that the LORD allows the Israelites to practice divination and observe times like the nations they will possess.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:14 states the LORD has not suffered the Israelites to do so, contrasting them with the nations that practice divination and observing times.

hard.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Deuteronomy Chapter 18.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18, what will the LORD do regarding a prophet like Moses?
options: Raise up a prophet from among their brethren
Make a new law for the people
questions.correctAnswer: Raise up a prophet from among their brethren
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:18 states that the LORD will raise up a prophet from among their brethren like Moses and put His words in his mouth.

questions.question: What consequence is stated for a prophet who speaks presumptuously in the name of the LORD or speaks in the name of other gods?
questions.correctAnswer: The prophet shall die
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:20 clearly states that a prophet who presumes to speak a word in the LORD's name without command, or who speaks in the name of other gods, shall die.

questions.question: How can one discern that a prophet has not spoken the word of the LORD according to Deuteronomy 18?
options: If the prophecy does not come to pass
If the prophet speaks at night
If the prophet uses complicated language
questions.correctAnswer: If the prophecy does not come to pass
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:22 instructs that if a prophet speaks in the LORD's name but the thing does not happen, then the LORD has not spoken it and the prophet spoke presumptuously.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 18:19 say will happen to those who do not hearken to the words spoken by the prophet in the LORD's name?
options: God will require it of them
They will receive a second chance
questions.correctAnswer: God will require it of them
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:19 warns that whoever does not listen to the words spoken by the prophet in God's name will be held accountable by God.

questions.question: What was the people's request at Horeb that is mentioned in Deuteronomy 18:16?
options: To not hear God's voice or see fire again
questions.correctAnswer: To not hear God's voice or see fire again
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:16 recounts the people asking to no longer hear the voice of God or see the great fire, fearing they would die.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the forbidden practices in Deuteronomy 18?
questions.correctAnswer: Eating unclean animals
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:10-11 lists prohibited practices like child sacrifice, divination, enchantment, witchcraft, but eating unclean animals is not mentioned in this chapter.

questions.question: True or False: Deuteronomy 18 teaches that the Levites shall have an inheritance among their brethren.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:1-2 clearly states that the Levites shall have no part nor inheritance among Israel, for the LORD is their inheritance.

questions.question: True or False: The phrase 'put my words in his mouth' in Deuteronomy 18:18 is an example of a literary device called a metaphor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:18 uses the metaphor of 'putting words in the mouth' to describe divine inspiration given to the prophet.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the promise of a prophet like Moses raised up by God as in Deuteronomy 18:15-18?
questions.explanation: Acts 3:22-23 quotes Deuteronomy 18:15-18, identifying Jesus as the prophet like Moses whom God raised up.

questions.question: What significant Hebrew word meaning relates to the term 'necromancer' in Deuteronomy 18:11, and why is it forbidden?
options: One who consults the dead; forbidden because it seeks knowledge apart from God
One who heals the sick; forbidden due to pagan rituals
One who predicts the weather; forbidden because of false prophecy
One who leads sacrifices; forbidden due to idolatry
questions.correctAnswer: One who consults the dead; forbidden because it seeks knowledge apart from God
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term translated 'necromancer' refers to one who communicates with spirits of the dead, which is abominable to God as per Deuteronomy 18:11-12.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 18:17 states, 'They have well spoken that which they have spoken.' To whom is this referring and what does it imply about the people's request?
options: It refers to the people's request for a prophet, meaning God approves their desire
It refers to Moses' complaints about the people, meaning God disapproves
It refers to the priests' demands for offerings, meaning God is neutral
It refers to the king's commands, meaning God questions their authority
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to the people's request for a prophet, meaning God approves their desire
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:17 confirms that God agrees the people's request not to hear His voice directly but through a prophet is well spoken.

questions.question: What is the role of the Levites according to Deuteronomy 18:6-7 when they come to the place the LORD chooses?
options: To minister in the name of the LORD as their brethren do
questions.correctAnswer: To minister in the name of the LORD as their brethren do
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:6-7 describes that Levites who come to the LORD’s chosen place shall minister in His name alongside their brethren.

questions.question: Which theme in Deuteronomy 18 is fulfilled by Jesus Christ in the New Testament?
options: The promise of a prophet like Moses
questions.correctAnswer: The promise of a prophet like Moses
questions.explanation: Jesus is identified in Acts 3:22 as the prophet like Moses that God promised in Deuteronomy 18:15-18, fulfilling this theme.

questions.question: Deuteronomy 18:13 exhorts the people to be 'perfect with the LORD thy God.' What does this imply in the context of the chapter?
options: To be blameless and obedient, avoiding forbidden practices
To be flawless in sacrifices only
To isolate from all other nations
questions.correctAnswer: To be blameless and obedient, avoiding forbidden practices
questions.explanation: In context, Deuteronomy 18:13 calls for moral and religious perfection by shunning abominable practices listed earlier.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18 reflect the historical context of the ancient Near East regarding forbidden practices?
options: It forbids practices common among surrounding nations, such as child sacrifice and divination
It encourages adopting foreign religious customs
It mandates worship of multiple gods
It promotes political alliances through religious syncretism
questions.correctAnswer: It forbids practices common among surrounding nations, such as child sacrifice and divination
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:9-12 condemns abominable practices prevalent in neighboring nations, reflecting Israel's call to be distinct.

theological.title: Deuteronomy Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Deuteronomy Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:1, what do the priests, the Levites, and all the tribe of Levi receive instead of a land inheritance among Israel?
options: They eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire and his inheritance
They receive a double portion of land
They receive silver and gold as inheritance
They inherit the cities of refuge
questions.correctAnswer: They eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire and his inheritance
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:1 states that the Levites have no part nor inheritance with Israel but shall eat the offerings of the LORD made by fire and his inheritance, indicating their spiritual and sacrificial provision rather than land.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 18:2 give for the Levites having no inheritance among their brethren?
options: They are not part of Israel
They refused to fight in wars
They chose not to settle in the land
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is their inheritance
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:2 explains that the Levites have no inheritance among their brethren because the LORD Himself is their inheritance, signifying their unique priestly role dependent on God.

questions.question: What specific parts of the sacrifice are given to the priests as their due according to Deuteronomy 18:3?
options: The shoulder, the two cheeks, and the maw
The head, the feet, and the tail
The heart, the liver, and the kidneys
The horns, the hooves, and the hide
questions.correctAnswer: The shoulder, the two cheeks, and the maw
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:3 details that the priest's due from the people offering sacrifices includes the shoulder, the two cheeks, and the maw, symbolizing specific portions set apart for the priests.

questions.question: What offerings besides parts of sacrifices does Deuteronomy 18:4 instruct the people to give to the priests?
options: The firstfruit of corn, wine, oil, and the first of the fleece of sheep
The entire harvest and all animals
questions.correctAnswer: The firstfruit of corn, wine, oil, and the first of the fleece of sheep
questions.explanation: According to Deuteronomy 18:4, the people are to give the firstfruit of their corn, wine, oil, and the first of the fleece of their sheep to the priests, emphasizing the offering of the first and best to God’s ministers.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning God’s choice and priesthood is taught in Deuteronomy 18:5?
options: God chose the Levites to minister in His name forever
All tribes have equal priestly roles
Only kings can minister before God
questions.correctAnswer: God chose the Levites to minister in His name forever
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:5 teaches the doctrine of divine election, stating that the LORD chose the Levites out of all tribes to minister in His name perpetually, indicating God’s sovereign call and covenantal priesthood.

questions.question: What prohibition against pagan practices is emphasized in Deuteronomy 18:10?
options: No one is to practice divination, witchcraft, or passing children through the fire
No one is to eat unclean animals
No one is to wear mixed fabrics
No one is to plant two kinds of seeds in one field
questions.correctAnswer: No one is to practice divination, witchcraft, or passing children through the fire
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:10 explicitly prohibits several pagan practices such as making children pass through fire, divination, and witchcraft, marking these as abominations to the LORD.

questions.question: What does Deuteronomy 18:12 teach about the nature of occult practices in relation to God?
options: They are abominations and cause God to drive out those nations
They are acceptable if done secretly
They are a form of worship pleasing to God
They are neutral practices without consequence
questions.correctAnswer: They are abominations and cause God to drive out those nations
questions.explanation: Verse 12 teaches that all who practice occult arts are abominations to the LORD, and because of these abominations, God drives out those nations, demonstrating His holiness and judgment against sin.

questions.question: What is the key command regarding personal holiness in Deuteronomy 18:13?
options: Thou shalt be perfect with the LORD thy God
Thou shalt keep the Sabbath holy
Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself
questions.correctAnswer: Thou shalt be perfect with the LORD thy God
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:13 commands Israel to be perfect (blameless, wholehearted) with the LORD, emphasizing the call to holiness and covenant faithfulness before God.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18:15 describe the prophet that the LORD will raise up from among Israel?
options: A prophet like Moses, from among their brethren, whom they shall hearken to
A foreign prophet who will bring new laws
A priest who will replace the Levites
A king who will lead them to battle
questions.correctAnswer: A prophet like Moses, from among their brethren, whom they shall hearken to
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:15 prophesies that God will raise a prophet like Moses from among the brethren, to whom the people must listen, revealing the promise of a divinely appointed mediator.

questions.question: What reason does Deuteronomy 18:18 give for God raising up a prophet like Moses?
options: To put His words in the prophet’s mouth and command him to speak all He commands
To give new laws replacing the Torah
To lead Israel into military conquest
questions.correctAnswer: To put His words in the prophet’s mouth and command him to speak all He commands
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:18 reveals that God will raise a prophet like Moses, putting His words in his mouth so that the prophet will speak all God commands, emphasizing divine revelation and authority.

questions.question: According to Deuteronomy 18:20, what is the consequence for a prophet who presumptuously speaks in God’s name without His command?
options: That prophet shall be forgiven if he repents
That prophet shall become a priest
questions.correctAnswer: That prophet shall die
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:20 states that any prophet who speaks presumptuously in God's name without command or who speaks in the name of other gods shall die, underscoring the seriousness of true prophecy.

questions.question: How does Deuteronomy 18:22 instruct the people to test a prophet’s authenticity?
options: If what the prophet says in God’s name does not come to pass, he has spoken presumptuously
If the prophet is wealthy and honored
If the prophet speaks in parables
questions.correctAnswer: If what the prophet says in God’s name does not come to pass, he has spoken presumptuously
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:22 teaches that a prophet’s words must be tested by their fulfillment; if the prophecy does not come true, the prophet has spoken presumptuously and is not to be feared.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God’s provision and priestly ministry can be drawn from Deuteronomy 18:1-2 and 18:6-8?
options: God provides for the Levites spiritually and materially as His inheritance, regardless of land possession
The Levites must purchase land to serve as priests
Only Levites born in the central sanctuary can minister
The Levites receive land inheritance equal to other tribes
questions.correctAnswer: God provides for the Levites spiritually and materially as His inheritance, regardless of land possession
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:1-2 declares that the Levites have no land inheritance because the LORD is their inheritance, and 18:6-8 explains that Levites who come to minister receive portions and sustenance, highlighting God’s provision beyond land.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about divine revelation and prophecy is synthesized from Deuteronomy 18:15-19?
options: God promises a prophet like Moses who will speak His words, and rejecting his message incurs divine judgment
Prophets can speak independently of God’s command
Prophecy is not necessary for Israel’s guidance
Every person can be a prophet without divine appointment
questions.correctAnswer: God promises a prophet like Moses who will speak His words, and rejecting his message incurs divine judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 15-19 articulate that God will raise a prophet like Moses to speak His commands, and refusal to heed his words results in accountability to God, affirming the doctrine of authoritative prophecy and judgment.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed in His judgment against occult practices as described in Deuteronomy 18:12?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and justice
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 18:12 shows that God abhors occult practices and drives out nations committing them, demonstrating His holiness in separating from sin and His justice in punishing disobedience (cf. Isaiah 59:2).
